title: 2003 AMC 12B Problem 24
statement: Positive integers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are chosen so that \(a \lt b \lt c,\) and the system of equations \[2x + y = 2003\] and \[ \begin{aligned} &y = |x - a| + |x - b| \\ &\quad {}+ |x - c| \end{aligned} \] has exactly one solution. What is the minimum value of \(c?\)

solutions.text:
The function \(y = |x-a| + |x-b| + |x-c|\) is piecewise linear with slopes \(-3, -1, 1, 3\) and corners at \(x = a, b, c.\) The line \(2x + y = 2003\) has slope \(-2.\)

A line of slope \(-2\) meets this graph exactly once only if it passes through the leftmost corner \((a,\, b + c - 2a),\) where the graph’s slope jumps from \(-3\) to \(-1.\) Substituting, \[ 2a + (b + c - 2a) = 2003, \] so \(b + c = 2003.\)

Since \(b \lt c,\) we need \(c \gt \dfrac{2003}{2},\) so \(c \ge 1002.\) This bound is attained: take \(a = 1,\) \(b = 1001,\) and \(c = 1002.\) Therefore the minimum is \(1002.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The graph of \(y = |x-a| + |x-b| + |x-c|\) is piecewise linear with slopes \(-3, -1, 1, 3\)
The line has slope \(-2;\) a single intersection forces it to touch the corner at \(x = a,\) where \(y = b + c - 2a\)
